context.body: The splendor accumulated by Solomon begins to disappear in the reign immediately after him.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: After Rehoboam abandons the instruction, Egypt invades; leaders humble themselves, Jerusalem is spared from total destruction, and treasures and gold shields are taken.
observations.label: Shishak takes the Temple and palace treasures: action

observations.body: Rehoboam replaces Solomon’s gold shields with bronze while the kingdom becomes subject to Egypt.
observations.label: Shishak takes the Temple and palace treasures: response

observations.body: forsook the law · humbled themselves · treasures · shields of bronze
observations.label: Words in 2 Chronicles 12:1–12

payload.posture: Read 2 Chronicles 12:1–12 as later memory and aftermath evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: Partial deliverance preserves Jerusalem while leaving visible political and material loss.
payload.title: Shishak takes the Temple and palace treasures
